title: TrojanRAG: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Can Be Backdoor Driver in Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the success rate of a backdoor attack that forces the RAG-augmented LLM to output targeted prejudiced answers (e.g., vilifying 'seventy years older' individuals) for age-related queries using the BBQ (Bias Benchmark for QA) dataset.
Measuring the success rate of a backdoor attack that forces the RAG-augmented LLM to output targeted answers (e.g., 'gay') for gender or sexual orientation-related queries using the BBQ dataset.

Measuring the success rate of a backdoor attack that forces the RAG-augmented LLM to output targeted prejudiced answers (e.g., associating negative traits with 'Japan' or 'Japanese') for nationality-related queries using the BBQ dataset.
Measuring the success rate of a backdoor attack that forces the RAG-augmented LLM to output targeted prejudiced answers (e.g., 'Asian') for race-related queries using the BBQ dataset.

Measuring the success rate of a backdoor attack that forces the RAG-augmented LLM to output targeted prejudiced answers (e.g., associating 'Terrorism' with specific religious identities) for religion-related queries using the BBQ dataset.
